rationale:
bugs_open/308: the misdirected_cta detector and the CTA repairer answer 'which pages may be a CTA destination?' from different sources, so 200 findings (re-measured live 2026-08-22, up from the filed 149) name a repair no writer can perform. 112 of them sit on work items the platform marked COMPLETE — the repair ran, reported success and changed nothing.

The blocker is that CTA provenance is DERIVED, not recorded (LNK-033): 'no resolver path can produce a utility-area destination, therefore a stored valid one was authored'. Fixing 308 means letting labels resolve INTO utility pages, which falsifies that invariant directly — and then both of bugs_open/248's keep-branches would freeze the resolver's own output, with the detector arm that would have noticed already demoted. The OWNER RULED on 2026-08-18 (recorded in the bug file): build the real provenance record — fix candidate 1 — provenance FIRST, then the widening; and no opt-out flags.

THIS SUBMISSION IS PHASE A ONLY: record the provenance and re-base the predicate on it. It is behaviour-preserving by construction — with zero stamps in the DB and today's narrow candidate set the resolver never mints a utility url, so the new conjunct never fires. PHASE B (deleting candidatesFromHubs' filter, one shared candidate universe for detector and repairer, stopword recalibration, and a completion verifier) is a SEPARATE submission gated on this one being pod-verified live. I am naming it here rather than letting a reviewer discover it: Phase B retires LNK-033's invariant deliberately, and that retirement is the owner's 2026-08-18 ruling, not this lane's choice. Per the 2026-07-29 ruling I claim NO ordering constraint — I could not hold this out of the fleet if I wanted to.

Design pivot worth reviewing hardest: the stamp is VALUE-BOUND (it records WHICH url was minted, per field, not a boolean). That is what makes 8 of RFC_042's 9 content_data writers correct with zero code changes, and it is the only version that survives the section-editor MERGE case — under a boolean stamp a surviving stamp would licence the recompute to clobber a human's edit, which is bugs_open/248 all over again.

── ROUND 2 (resubmit of e4336931). Round 1 returned REVISE, gated by editquality. Every objection
is answered by a CHANGE, not an argument, and two of them found real defects. The code is written
and tested; this round reviews what is actually in the tree.

editquality #1 (HIGH — the non-page keep has no stamp hunk): the objection is right that the
plan's prose was self-contradictory, and the resolution is the opposite of what the prose implied.
The NON-PAGE KEEP MUST NOT STAMP. tel:/mailto:/external destinations are authored by construction
(IsAuthoredNonPageCTADestination), and that branch's write is a URI REPAIR of an authored value,
not a mint. Stamping it would make a genuine phone button recomputable — bugs_open/299's exact
defect. My edit-3 rationale wrongly listed it among the branches to stamp; the prose was wrong,
the intent was not. Corrected below and stated in the code.

editquality #2 (MEDIUM — the authored-utility keep's guard is dead code): CORRECT, and removed.
Reaching that branch proves storedCTADestinationIsAuthored returned true, which now REQUIRES
!CTAMintedCovers — so the guard could never fire. There is no stamp on that branch and the code
says why in place.

editquality #3 (MEDIUM — no analogous fallthrough re-stamp in applyCTARecompute): answered by
reading the persist rather than by symmetry. The rerender MERGES (mergedContent = stored ⊕ fresh,
rerender_page_sections_action.go:725-733), so an untouched field keeps its value AND its record
together; only the build path's DELETE+INSERT loses it. Stated in the code at that branch.

bug_historian #1 (HIGH — read the persist path before merge, 'owed' is not a control): DONE, and
the seat was right to insist. save_page_sections_action.go:968-1001 marshals the WHOLE map
(json.Marshal(section.ContentData)) with no key filtering, and extractSectionsFromMetadata:1354
takes m["content_data"] wholesale. No declared-key filter anywhere on that path. This is no longer
inferred from the 16-row measurement; the measurement now corroborates a code read.

reuse_agent (MEDIUM — was an existing content_data metadata sidecar checked?): checked, and the
answer sharpens the design rather than changing it. There is NO generic per-field provenance
helper (searched datahelpers/actions/internal/pkg for FieldProvenance/StampField/ValueProvenance/
MarkResolved/RecordFieldSource — zero hits). sections_metadata is the transport array, not a
sidecar. But the `__` PREFIX IS an established convention, not a new one: 15 distinct `__` markers
already live in platform/orchestration, and content_data_envelope_guard.go's isEnvelopeMarkerKey
already treats ANY `__` key as a platform marker rather than content. So this extends an existing
convention.

guardian #2 (MEDIUM — could an envelope guard's allow-list refuse saves fleet-wide?): READ, and
the risk does not exist. content_data_envelope_guard.go keys on the envelope SIGNATURE (type ==
"text" AND a STRING result), explicitly NOT on key arity or an allow-list — its own header says
"Key on the signature, never the arity". A nested-map key passes untouched. One real interaction
found and now documented: isEnvelopeMarkerKey DROPS any `__` key when decoding a poisoned row, so
a record on such a row is lost by that rescue — rare (2 rows fleet-wide) and in the safe direction
(→ authored → frozen, never → recomputable).

guardian #1 (MEDIUM — third caller of the changed signature?): settled by the compiler. The
signature change is unexported and `go build ./platform/...` is clean, so the two writers plus the
tests are the whole caller set; a third would not compile.

guidelines (MEDIUM — register entry in the SAME commit): DONE. LNK-035 added and LNK-033 AMENDED
visibly (its invariant is retired by owner ruling, not quietly broken), both in the commit that
ships this code, plus the index row.

debug_historian (MEDIUM — name the pod-verification symbol and control): grep the running binary
for `__cta_minted` (must be present) with a control string this change did NOT add (must be
absent) in the same exec, per service; then `SELECT count(*) FROM page_components WHERE
content_data ? '__cta_minted'` must move 0→N after an induced build AND an induced cta_links_stale
rerender — one of each, because the two writers are independent.

bug_historian #2 / prior_art (LOW — cite bugs_closed/097 and bugs_closed/023; note both are
CLOSED, the objection said bugs_open/097): read. Neither shape reopens: an unbuilt-page target can
neither be stamped nor read as authored, because every write branch AND the predicate itself
require validPages.Contains, which an unbuilt page fails.

AND ONE DEFECT I FOUND MYSELF, which is new in this round and is why the edit list has changed:
the persist merges SHALLOWLY and the record is a NESTED MAP, so a resolved_data stamping one slot
REPLACED the stored record and dropped the sibling slot's — freezing it. Four of six ctaFieldNames
components have two slots, so it is the common case. SeedCTAMinted is the fix. It lives INSIDE
both writers rather than in the callers' loops because a loop-level call was mutation-tested and
proved DELETABLE with every test in the tree still green. A second helper (CarryCTAMinted) was
written for the unresolved fallthrough and then DELETED as redundant — mutation showed removing it
changed no test, because the seed had already carried the record. Two guards in series with one
dead is how an unexercised branch ships.

plan.summary: Record CTA destination provenance as a value-bound reserved key in page_components.content_data (__cta_minted: {url_field: minted_url}), written by BOTH resolver writers on every branch that MINTS a url, seeded per section so a shallow merge cannot drop a sibling slot's record, and consumed by re-basing storedCTADestinationIsAuthored — whose SIGNATURE changes so no caller can use the shape test without the mint check. The non-page keep and the authored-utility keep deliberately do NOT stamp. No config key, no migration, no backfill.

edits.rationale: The provenance vocabulary, in datahelpers because BOTH writers (actions package) and any future check need it, and because actions imports datahelpers but not vice versa — the same placement reason links_tel.go (LNK-034) and ctafields.go already use. Pure functions, no DB, no config surface at all: per the owner's 'no opt-out flags' ruling there is nothing here a caller can switch off. Comparison is via NormalizePagePath so /contact.html and /contact/index.html cannot disagree — the same normaliser the keeps and the detector already share. ROUND 2: adds SeedCTAMinted, which exists for a defect found during implementation — both persist paths merge SHALLOWLY and this key is a NESTED map, so a record for one slot replaced the stored record and dropped the sibling's, freezing it. Four of six ctaFieldNames components have two slots. Seeding is safe ONLY because the stamp is value-bound: a seeded entry naming a url the field no longer carries reads as authored, not as a false mint. Reuse checked (reuse_agent): no generic per-field provenance helper exists anywhere in the tree, but the `__` prefix is an ESTABLISHED convention — 15 distinct `__` markers already live in platform/orchestration, and content_data_envelope_guard.go's isEnvelopeMarkerKey already treats any `__` key as a platform marker rather than content.

Re-base the predicate on the record. The SIGNATURE change is the enforcement, not decoration: taking (stored, field) instead of a bare url means no caller can reach the utility-area shape test without also passing the map the mint check reads. A caller that only has a url string will not compile — which is the compile-time version of 'a comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share' (owner, 2026-08-02). Validity stays load-bearing: an INVALID /contact.html is bugs_open/203's phantom and replacing it is the repair, pinned by an existing test.

Stamp on the branches that MINT a url — the label match and the positional pick — and NOT on the two keeps. ROUND 1 CORRECTION (editquality #1, HIGH): my previous rationale listed the non-page keep among the branches to stamp. That was wrong. tel:/mailto:/external destinations are authored by construction and that branch's write is a URI REPAIR of an authored value; stamping it would make a genuine phone button recomputable, which is bugs_open/299's defect. The authored-utility keep does not stamp either, and the reason is structural rather than a choice (editquality #2, correct): reaching it PROVES the record does not cover the value, because storedCTADestinationIsAuthored returns false as soon as it does — a conditional re-stamp there was dead code and has been removed. SeedCTAMinted is called at the TOP of this function, not once per section in the caller's loop, because a loop-level call was mutation-tested and proved deletable with every test in the tree still green. That seed also subsumes the unresolved fallthrough: a carried value equals the stored one by construction, so the seeded entry covers it — a separate re-stamp there was written and then deleted as redundant, mutation-verified.
edits.sketch:
@@ setCTAField, top @@
 	if field == "" {
 		return
 	}
+	// The persist merges SHALLOWLY and the record is a nested map, so stamping
+	// only THIS field would replace the stored record and drop the sibling
+	// slot's. Inside the function, not the caller's loop: a loop-level call
+	// proved deletable with every test green.
+	datahelpers.SeedCTAMinted(resolved, stored)
@@ label-match branch (MINTS) @@
 			resolved[field] = match.URL
+			datahelpers.SetCTAMinted(resolved, field, match.URL)
@@ bugs_open/248 authored-utility keep — NO stamp, deliberately @@
+		// NO MINT STAMP HERE, and its absence is load-bearing: reaching this
+		// branch PROVES the record does not cover storedURL.
 		resolved[field] = storedURL
@@ bugs_open/299 non-page keep — NO stamp, deliberately @@
  		// (unchanged) tel:/mailto: are authored by construction; this write is
  		// a URI repair, not a mint. Stamping would make a phone button recomputable.
@@ positional pick (MINTS) @@
 		resolved[field] = target.URL
+		datahelpers.SetCTAMinted(resolved, field, target.URL)
@@ unresolved fallthrough @@
+	// No re-stamp needed: the seed above already carried the record, and a
+	// carried value equals the stored one by construction.

edits.rationale: The repair-path writer, kept in lockstep. KEEP #1 consumes the new predicate; KEEP #2/#3 and their ORDER are untouched (LNK-034's mutation-proven seam). Same seed at the top, for the same shallow-merge reason. ROUND 1 (editquality #3): this writer needs NO fallthrough re-stamp, and that is read rather than assumed — the rerender MERGES (mergedContent = stored ⊕ fresh, rerender_page_sections_action.go:725-733), so an untouched field keeps its value AND its record together; only the build path's DELETE+INSERT loses it. Neither keep stamps, for the same reasons as the build path.
edits.sketch:
@@ applyCTARecompute, label-match branch @@
 			resolved[field] = match.URL
+			datahelpers.SetCTAMinted(resolved, field, match.URL)
@@ applyCTARecompute, KEEP #1 @@
-	if hasCurrent && storedCTADestinationIsAuthored(current, validPages) &&
+	if hasCurrent && storedCTADestinationIsAuthored(stored, field, validPages) &&
 		datahelpers.NormalizePagePath(current) != datahelpers.NormalizePagePath(pageURL) {
@@ applyCTARecompute, positional pick @@
 	resolved[field] = target.URL
+	datahelpers.SetCTAMinted(resolved, field, target.URL)

edits.rationale: Unit-pins the value-binding, which is the design's load-bearing property. Includes the normalisation boundary (/contact.html vs /contact/index.html must be the SAME value) and the absent-stamp default (false — the no-backfill guarantee). MUTATION PROOF: make CTAMintedCovers presence-bound (ignore the url) and TestStaleStampDoesNotCoverEditedValue fails — that is the section-editor clobber.

The asymmetry pin is UNCHANGED in this phase — bugs_open/308's verification bar #2 says that if that test is edited without provenance landing, the fix is wrong, so it stays byte-identical here and is rewritten only in Phase B, after the stamp is pod-verified. Its call sites are updated for the new signature only. New cases: a minted utility destination is RE-DERIVABLE (mutation: drop the !CTAMintedCovers conjunct -> this fails, and it is the LNK-033 landmine as a test); an unstamped stored utility url is still KEPT (248 unregressed); a carried value at the unresolved fallthrough keeps its stamp (mutation: delete the fallthrough re-stamp -> this fails).

grounded_in: bugs_open/308 OWNER RULINGS 2026-08-18: 'Build the provenance record. Fix candidate 1 is the chosen route.' and 'No opt-out flags. Don't add any new flags that let other agents ignore things — this leads to bugs.'

Re-measured live 2026-08-22: the bug file's own query returns 200 findings (filed at 149 on 2026-08-17), split complete 71 items/112 findings, unresolved 53/86, cancelled 2/2 — the 112 are repairs that ran, reported success and changed nothing.

DEMAND CONTROL, same day: SELECT date_trunc('day',created_at), count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE item_key LIKE 'misdirected_cta:%' returns 2026-08-19: 3, 08-18: 128, 08-17: 208 — the detector has been silent for three days, so 200 is a STOCK not a flow and no post-fix count is evidence until a discovery run is induced.

resolve_internal_links_action.go:674-676 (storedCTADestinationIsAuthored) — 'THE INVARIANT: no resolver path can produce a utility-area destination... A stored url that is BOTH a valid page AND in a utility area was therefore not written by setCTAField or applyCTARecompute.' This is the derived provenance being replaced.

The design's load-bearing assumption MEASURED, not assumed, and grouped so it could have come out otherwise: 16 rows across FOUR component functions (content-block-about 12, gauntlet-cta 2, archetype-combinations 1, archetype-grid 1) store a *_target_title key their input_schema does NOT declare (bool_or over content_components.input_schema = f). Counting the 844 total would have proven nothing — 438 sit on hero/call-to-action, which DO declare it. So an undeclared resolver key survives into stored content_data.

The __ namespace is clean fleet-wide: SELECT jsonb_object_keys over page_components.content_data LIKE '\_\_%' returns 0 rows (underscores escaped — unescaped, _ is a LIKE wildcard and the query returns every key).

resolve_internal_links_action.go:207-212 — setCTAField is handed `existing` from loadExistingSectionContentData, a FRESH page_components read, while the PBP-039 carry's output is the separate `resolved` argument. This is why the stamp fix belongs in setCTAField and PBP-039's carry is untouched.

setCTAField's final branch appends to *unresolved and writes NOTHING to resolved[field]; every other branch assigns it. RFC_042 §2 records the plan->save funnel as DELETE+INSERT (REPLACE), so a carried value surviving that branch is persisted without the previous cycle's stamp.

rerender_page_sections_action.go:1057-1065 — '⚠ THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: this branch is reachable only because keep #2's predicate requires validPages.Contains'. KEEP #2/#3 and their order are deliberately untouched by this change.

Consumer enumeration by symbol sweep (not assertion): loadContentHubs/loadInteractivePages have THREE non-test callers — resolve_internal_links_action.go, rerender_page_sections_action.go, and render_site_components_action.go:182-190 (the site HEADER CTA fallback), which no CTA bug file or register entry names. Phase B therefore widens at the candidate-assembly seam and NOT at the loaders; site_components stores 0 cta_url keys across all 24 header rows, so a content_data diff could not have seen a header regression.

PERSIST PATH READ, not inferred (bug_historian's HIGH objection): save_page_sections_action.go:968-1001 does `json.Marshal(section.ContentData)` of the WHOLE map and inserts it as $6::jsonb — no declared-key filter; extractSectionsFromMetadata:1354 takes m["content_data"] wholesale. So an undeclared key reaches the column by construction, and the 16-row *_target_title measurement corroborates a code read rather than substituting for one.

ENVELOPE GUARD READ (guardian's fleet-wide-refusal objection): content_data_envelope_guard.go's isLLMTransportEnvelope keys on the SIGNATURE — type == "text" AND a STRING result — and its own header states 'Key on the signature, never the arity'. There is no allow-list of top-level content_data keys anywhere on the write path, so a new nested-map key cannot cause a refusal. ONE real interaction: isEnvelopeMarkerKey(k) returns true for ANY "__" prefix and the decode DROPS such keys, so a record on an envelope-poisoned row is lost by that rescue — 2 such rows fleet-wide, none minted since mid-July, and the loss direction is safe (authored/frozen, never recomputable).

REUSE CHECK (reuse_agent): no generic per-field provenance mechanism exists — grep for FieldProvenance/StampField/ValueProvenance/MarkResolved/RecordFieldSource across platform/, internal/, pkg/ returns zero. sections_metadata is the transport array, not a sidecar. The `__` prefix is an existing convention: 15 distinct `__`-prefixed markers in platform/orchestration (__execution_context__, __step_error, __json_contract_unmet, ...).

RERENDER MERGE READ (editquality #3): rerender_page_sections_action.go:725-733 builds mergedContent = stored then fresh, key by key — 'Persisted content_data = stored ⊕ fresh resolved_data'. An untouched field keeps value and record together on the repair path; only the build path's DELETE+INSERT (RFC_042 §2) loses them, which is why only setCTAField needed the seed for that reason.

MUTATION PROOFS RUN in a scratch tree built from `git archive HEAD` (the working tree does not compile — another session's flag_page_image_rebuild_action.go is mid-edit): presence-bound CTAMintedCovers fails 5 tests across both packages; dropping the !CTAMintedCovers conjunct fails TestStoredCTADestinationIsAuthored; no-opping SeedCTAMinted inside setCTAField fails TestSetCTAFieldPreservesSiblingSlotStamp; the same inside applyCTARecompute fails TestApplyCTARecomputePreservesSiblingSlotStamp. A loop-level seed call was proved DELETABLE with every test green, which is why both calls live inside the functions.

bugs_closed/097 (cta_integrity_misses_card_links_to_unbuilt_pages) and bugs_closed/023 (cta_label_url_pairing_unchecked) — both CLOSED, not open as the round-1 objection had it. Neither shape reopens: every stamping branch AND storedCTADestinationIsAuthored itself require validPages.Contains, which an unbuilt page fails, so an unbuilt target can neither be stamped nor read as authored.

REGISTER (guidelines): LNK-035 added and LNK-033 AMENDED visibly in the same commit — the amendment states that the invariant is RETIRED by owner ruling rather than quietly broken, and corrects the landmine's own wording, which listed 'widen the loaders' and 'drop candidatesFromHubs' filter' as interchangeable when the loaders have a third consumer (the site header CTA fallback).
plan.risks:
1) FREEZE RESIDUAL — any path carrying a minted value without its record yields a false 'authored'. Now bounded to the envelope-decode rescue path (2 rows fleet-wide). Safe by direction: the label match runs AHEAD of every keep in both writers, so a frozen link whose copy names another page is still repaired. Disconfirming observation: a page_component_history pair where a utility-valid field was stamped in generation N and unstamped-same-value in N+1.
2) SHALLOW-MERGE SIBLING LOSS — found and fixed this round (SeedCTAMinted). Disconfirming observation: a two-CTA component whose stored record holds one slot after a pass that touched the other.
3) The record reaching rendered HTML or a writer prompt. Disconfirming observation: fleet grep of rendered_html for __cta_minted must return 0 after the roll. [ASSUMED] no template ranges over content_data keys — this is the one assumption left unread, and the grep is its cheap test.
4) The RFC_042/355 content-loss lane widening its differ to all keys and reading record churn as loss. Prevented by the key being deliberately NOT schema-declared; a CONTRIB into their NOTES names it.
5) Phase B, NOT in this submission, retires LNK-033's invariant and needs its stopword recalibration measured, not assumed — 'about' was deliberately kept out of LabelStopwords in the 2026-08-08 calibration.
6) POD VERIFICATION is the gate for Phase B and is now specified: grep the running binary for __cta_minted with a control string this change did not add, per service; then the content_data ? '__cta_minted' count must move 0->N after an induced build AND an induced cta_links_stale rerender.
